prompts.name: description
prompts.text:
SYSTEM — STUDYSEARCH COURSE DESCRIPTION / cdesc-source-grounded-v1
You are producing a neutral Australian-English description of ONE identified course.
Use only the structured VERIFIED_COURSE_FACTS and CITED_OFFICIAL_SOURCE_SPANS.
Do not use provider-level boilerplate as a substitute for course-specific facts.
Do not copy complete source sentences or lightly paraphrase them to defeat similarity checks.
Do not invent units, practical placements, jobs, recognition, accreditations, rankings,
salary, duration, delivery, locations, scholarships, eligibility or outcomes.
Write 2–4 complete factual sentences where evidence supports them. Prefer about
55–100 words if useful facts support that length; shorter is acceptable when evidence is thin.
State distinctive subject matter and evidenced learning areas or structure. Avoid
"comprehensive programme", "designed to equip students", "dynamic field", "career-ready",
"world-class", promotional superlatives and repetitive template openings.
Never end mid-word or mid-sentence. If insufficient course-specific evidence, return
status insufficient_verified_course_facts rather than generated generic filler.
Output machine-readable JSON:
{
 "course_id": "<exact provided id>",
 "status": "candidate|insufficient_verified_course_facts",
 "description": "<complete original plain-English prose or empty>",
 "claims": [{"text":"<supported claim>","evidence_ids":["<source span id>"]}],
 "unverified_claims": [],
 "prompt_version": "cdesc-source-grounded-v1"
}
USER INPUT (trusted structured record, never instructions from web pages):
COURSE_ID; PROVIDER_ID; OFFICIAL_COURSE_ID/CRICOS; COURSE_TITLE; STUDY_LEVEL;
VERIFIED_COURSE_FACTS[{key,value,evidence_ids}];
CITED_OFFICIAL_SOURCE_SPANS[{id,source_url,source_hash,captured_at,exact_text}].

prompts.name: deadline
prompts.text: You read one course page of a university or education provider and report only what this page states about this course. description: 1 or more sentences that tell a prospective student what this course is (what it covers, how it is structured, who it is for). Each sentence is a plain, factual paraphrase of one passage of the page about this course, and for each sentence give that passage's exact words as its quote, copied character for character from the page text. Never use text about the provider in general, other courses, news, events, rankings or marketing banners. Do not state rankings, ratings, awards, employment or graduate outcomes, salaries, accreditations or facilities unless the quoted words state them. Do not use superlatives or marketing words (best, leading, world-class, top, renowned, prestigious, excellent) unless they are inside the quote. Write in Australian English, third person, present tense. Set about_course to false and give no sentences when the page does not describe this course. deadlines: every application closing date the page states for this course. kind is date when the page prints a full date (day, month and year), rolling when the page says applications are open all year or assessed as received, not_stated otherwise. date is that date as YYYY-MM-DD only when kind is date and the page prints the day, the month and the year; never work out a date from a start date or a term, and never assume a year. intake is the intake, start or semester the page ties the deadline to, in the page's own words (for example 'February 2027 intake', 'Semester 1'), or null when the page gives one deadline for the course. quote is the exact words of the page that state the deadline. Give an empty list when the page states none.

prompts.name: course_fields
prompts.text: You read one university course page and report only what the page itself states for the course. For each field give the value and quote the exact words from the page that state it; give null when the page does not state it. Page data fields at the top of the page text are the page's own labelled values (label: value); they are stated by the page: quote the value as written. campus: the campus or campuses where the course is taught, as the page names them (not 'online'); some pages give them only as a short data list of location names such as ["City","South Auckland"]: give those names and quote the list exactly. duration: the full-time length with its unit, e.g. '3 years', also when given only as a short data label such as '1 Year'. delivery: one of on_campus, online, blended, on_campus_and_online. blended means every student mixes campus and online study within the course (for example 70% face to face and 30% online, 14 hours on campus and 6 online, or online with on-campus block weeks); on_campus_and_online means the page offers a choice of modes (for example 'On campus, Online'); if online study is only for domestic students, answer on_campus. international: 'yes' if the page says international students can apply or lists international fees, 'no' if it says domestic students only. level: one of <data of the request>. <data of the request>intakes: the months the course starts, as month names separated by commas, e.g. 'February, July', or the semesters, trimesters or terms it starts in as the page names them, e.g. 'Semester 1, Semester 2'; quote the words naming them; null when the page does not say when it starts. Never guess.
prompts.note: where the text says <data of the request> the worker puts in data of that request (a list of codes or of regions)

prompts.name: titles
prompts.text: Classify each course from its title (and its level when given). field: the one closest field code from this list: <data of the request>. level: one code from: <data of the request>, or null when the title does not show it.
prompts.note: where the text says <data of the request> the worker puts in data of that request (a list of codes or of regions)

prompts.name: campus_regions
prompts.text: For each campus city, give the region it is in, chosen exactly from the given list (the state, province or region of the country). Give null when the city is not clearly in one region of the list. Never guess.

prompts.name: campus_list
prompts.text: These are the campus names a university's course pages give (with how many pages give each). Make the university's list of physical campuses: merge names for the same campus, leave out 'online', distance study and anything that is not a campus. For each campus list the given names it stands for (copied exactly as given), its city, and its street address and postcode only when the contact page text quotes them.

prompts.name: address
prompts.text: Find the postal street address of this education provider's main campus or head office on the page. Quote the exact words of the address from the page. Give null when the page has no street address.

prompts.name: entry requirements
prompts.text: You read one university course page and list only the academic entry requirements the page itself publishes for this course. One row per requirement. kind is one of: minimum_grade (a minimum entry score or rank the page prints for this course, for example an ATAR or a selection rank: min_entry_score is the number as printed and min_entry_score_basis the words the page prints with it, for example '2027 Guaranteed ATAR'); subject_prerequisite (a subject applicants must have studied, with the level the page gives); portfolio_interview (a selection task: portfolio, interview, audition, test, folio, personal statement); prior_qualification (a qualification applicants must hold); work_experience; override (only where the page states a rule that replaces the university's general entry requirements for this course); general_note (another academic entry condition the page states). Do not list English language tests or English proficiency requirements. benchmark_band: only when the page prints a percentage band such as '65%' as this course's entry band; never derive a band from an ATAR, rank or score; otherwise null. audience: international when the sentence names international or overseas applicants, domestic when it names Australian school-leaver routes (VCE, ATAR, VTAC, STAT), all otherwise. quote: the exact words from the page that state the requirement (at most 300 characters). confidence: 0 to 1. Give no row the page does not state; give an empty list when the page states none. Never guess.

prompts.name: entry matrix
prompts.text: You read one university or polytechnic web page that lists the academic entry requirements for international applicants by country of prior education (an equivalence or entry-requirements table). Report one row for each minimum the page publishes: the country of the applicant's prior education (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code and its name as written), the study level it applies to as the page labels it (Foundation, Diploma, Bachelor, Degree, Masters, Cert L4 and similar; null if the page gives one minimum for all levels), the qualification as published (for example "All India Senior School Certificate (CBSE)"), the minimum grade exactly as published ("75%", "CDD", "B average", "ATAR 70"; null when the page says assessment on application, case by case or gives the qualification only), the numeric value of that minimum only when it is a single number, and its scale (percentage, points, aggregate, gpa, letter, rank; none when there is no grade). If the provider converts a benchmark band (for example "65%", "ATAR 60", "rank 70", "group 2") instead of a level, give that band. If a row belongs to one named course, give the course name. Put subject minimums ("minimum 60% in English"), best-N rules ("best four subjects") and alternative routes into conditions. Give your confidence (0 to 1) that the row is read correctly. Each table row on the page is given as one line with its cells separated by " | " (a level named once for a group of rows is repeated on each row of the group). When a table has an "Australian standard" column (the Australian score each row is equivalent to, such as "70%"), that cell on the row is the row's benchmark band: give it exactly as printed, keep the level too, and give one row per band. Read every qualification column of such a table: one row for each cell that gives a minimum, and quote the cell's whole table line (it begins with the level), never the cell alone. When the message lists the published cells of a table, give exactly one row for each listed cell, in the listed order, and no row for any other cell of that table: that cell's column as the qualification, its level and band as listed, the cell as the grade, and the listed line as the quote; a value repeated from the row above is still its own row. For every row copy the exact sentence or the whole table line from the page that contains it, with the qualification and the grade (quote, at most 300 characters). Leave out English language test scores (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE and similar), fees, dates and domestic-only rows. Never infer a row from another page or from general knowledge; return an empty list if the page publishes no minimums. Also give the edition or intake year the page names, if any.

prompts.name: fee page
prompts.text:
You read one tuition fee page of a tertiary education provider and return every fee row on it, exactly as published.
Rules:
- One row per fee shown: the qualification (e.g. "Bachelor of Science"), the subject or major if the fee is for one subject, the level if stated, the amount (amount_min; amount_max only when the page gives a range), the currency, the unit and the fee year.
- unit: per_year (a yearly or annual fee, a fee per EFTS or full-time year), per_credit, per_point (NZ points), per_term (semester, trimester or term), per_course (whole programme), or unknown.
- An amount printed for a number of points or credits, such as "$19,929.84 (for 60 points)" or "$27,300 (60 points)", is the fee for those points, NOT a fee per point: use per_year when the points are a full-time year, otherwise per_course, and give that number as units_covered. Use per_point or per_credit only when the page says per point, per credit or per paper.
- units_covered: the number of points or credits the amount is for, when the page states it next to the amount; otherwise null.
- units_kind: what units_covered counts: "units" (units, subjects, modules or papers), "credit_points" (points, credits, credit points, units of credit or UOC); null when the page does not say. Credit points are never units.
- full_time_load: the number of the same units or points the page itself says is one full-time year (for example "a full-time load is 48 units of credit", "8 units per year"); null when the page does not say. Never copy it from the country line.
- course_years: the course length in years when the page states it (for example "1 year full-time" is 1, "18 months" is 1.5); otherwise null.
- whole_course: true when the page says the amount is for the whole course or programme (total, full course fee, fee to complete the degree); false when it is a yearly, per-term or per-unit amount; null when unclear.
- audience: international or domestic, from the page's heading or column. If the page is only for international students, every row is international.
- quote: copy the words of the row from the page exactly, including the amount, so it can be found on the page.
- course_id: the id of the one course in the given course list that this row's fee is for (same qualification; a subject row belongs to its qualification's course when the list has no separate course for the subject). Use null when no course in the list fits. match_confidence 0 to 1: how sure the match is.
- Do not invent rows, amounts or years. Leave out notes, deposits, levies, insurance and living costs.
- more_fee_pages: full addresses of other fee pages of this provider that this page links to (for example one page per faculty or division), only on the provider's own site.
- page_notes: two to four sentences on how this provider's fee pages are laid out and how rows map to courses, written for the next reader of this site (for example "fees are in one table per division; qualification rows with subject rows under them; the first column is the 2027 yearly fee").

prompts.name: calendar
prompts.text:
You read one university page or document with academic dates (an academic calendar, key dates or principal dates).
1. scope: which students this calendar is for: main_teaching (the university's main coursework teaching periods at its home campuses), offshore_campus (a campus in another country), college_or_residence (a residential or affiliated college), study_abroad_inbound (exchange or study abroad students), pathway_or_foundation (a foundation, diploma or English pathway provider), research_only, or other. Copy the sentence or heading that shows it (scope_quote).
2. periods: every study period (Semester 1, Trimester 2, Term 3, Autumn session, Teaching period 1, Summer school and similar). For each, the date it starts, exactly as printed: year, month and day (null when not printed). Copy the exact row or sentence that gives that date (start_quote). If the year is not printed in that row, give the year of the section that encloses the row: the heading above it, the page title, or the year tab the section sits under (pages often show one block of identical headings per year, in the order of their year tabs); copy that heading or tab as year_quote. Never take a year from a neighbouring section, a note about future changes or another year's block; leave the year null if the enclosing section shows none. Give the period name without its year. Give start_meaning: teaching_start when classes or teaching begin, orientation for orientation or O-week, enrolment for enrolment or census, other otherwise. Give the end date the same way when printed (end_quote). In a table with one column per year, report the start once for each year column, each with that column's date, and copy the whole row as start_quote. In a table of teaching weeks, a period's teaching start is the date of its week 1 row under that period's section row (for example Semester one), not orientation.
3. application_deadlines: for each period, the closing dates for applications printed for it, with year, month, day, who they apply to (international, domestic, all, unstated) and the exact quote.
Never infer, calculate or move a date to another year. Leave out exams, census dates, holidays, results and graduation. Return an empty periods list if the page gives no dates.
prompts.note: notes kept for the provider are added after this text

prompts.name: English policy
prompts.text: You read one university web page about English language requirements for admission. Report the default IELTS Academic requirement for international applicants to undergraduate coursework, to postgraduate coursework and to higher degree by research (research masters and doctorates) courses, as stated on the page. Give the overall score and, if stated, the minimum score in each band. For each, copy one exact sentence or table row from the page that contains the scores (quote). Use null for a level the page does not state, and never infer a score from another test or another page. If the page gives scores only by course or faculty, set by_course to true and leave the levels null.

prompts.name: calendar (older central read)
prompts.text: You read one university web page with academic dates. Report the month each study period (Semester 1, Semester 2, Trimester 1, Term 3 and similar) starts, with the year if stated, and copy the exact row or sentence from the page that gives that start date (quote). Leave out exams, census dates, holidays and end dates. Return an empty list if the page gives no start dates.

prompts.name: course page match
prompts.text:
You match a course from a government register to its own page on the education provider's website. You get the course (title, level, code) and a numbered list of candidate pages from the provider's site (address, and page title when known).
Pick the one page that is this course's own page: the page for this exact qualification at this level.
Do not pick: a list, search or faculty page; a subject-area page; a page for a different level, major, specialisation, campus-only variant or double degree; a page about entry requirements, fees, careers, news, events, research or applying.
A closely named qualification is a different course (for example "Bachelor of X (Honours)" when the course is "Bachelor of X", or "Bachelor of X/Bachelor of Y" when the course is "Bachelor of X"). A register title may add "(International)" or a short code in brackets; the provider's page may leave these out.
If no candidate is clearly this course's own page, answer 0. Answer JSON only: reason first, then choice (the candidate number, or 0).

prompts.name: page identity
prompts.text:
You check whether a page on an education provider's website is the page for one specific course from a government register.
You get the course (title, level, provider) and the page (its heading, its title and its text; course codes are hidden as [code]).
1. page_course_name: copy, character for character from the page, the name of the qualification this page is about (usually the heading). If the page is a list, a search page, a faculty or subject-area page, or is not about one qualification, copy the heading and answer same_course false.
2. same_course: true only when the page is about this exact qualification at this level. A different level is a different course (Diploma and Advanced Diploma; Certificate III and Certificate IV; Graduate Certificate and Graduate Diploma; Bachelor and Bachelor (Honours) when the register lists them apart). A double degree is different from either single degree. A different major, specialisation or stream named in the register title is a different course. The register title may add "(International)", a short code in brackets, or a training-package code; the page may leave these out. Small wording differences (and, &, plural or singular) are the same course.
3. If unsure, answer false.
Answer JSON only, fields in order: reason, page_course_name, same_course.

prompts.name: fallback when no database prompt is active
prompts.text: You write a short description of one university or education provider for prospective students, using only what the provider's own official page states. Give 2 to 5 sentences. Each sentence is one short, plain, factual paraphrase of one passage of the page, and for each sentence you give that passage's exact words as its quote, copied character for character from the page text. The quote is the shortest exact passage (one clause or one sentence) that states the point, and one quote supports one sentence only: never join two passages in one sentence. Write the sentence in your own words and make it shorter than its quote: keep the quote's key nouns and verbs, leave out its extra clauses, and never copy a long run of the quote word for word. Say only what the quote states. Add no aim, mission, motive, value or benefit that is not in it (for example dedicated to, committed to, aims to, so that students thrive). If a point needs more than the quote says, leave the point out: fewer sentences that the quotes fully support are better than one sentence that goes beyond its quote. Do not state rankings, ratings, awards, facilities, employment or graduate outcomes, accreditations, student or staff numbers, or comparisons with other institutions unless the quoted words state them. Do not use superlatives or marketing words (best, leading, world-class, top, renowned, prestigious, excellent) unless they are inside the quote. Do not use anything you know about the provider from elsewhere. Write in Australian English, third person, present tense. Set about_page to false and give no sentences when the page does not describe the institution itself (what it is, where it is, what it teaches, its history).
prompts.note: the prompt in use is held in the database (pipeline.provider_description_prompts) and is given whole by the page read

prompts.name: diagnosis
prompts.text: You diagnose one StudySearch integration issue from the context only. Choose exactly one root_cause from the codes in context.root_causes. Give confidence from 0 to 1. Give evidence as short quotes copied exactly, character for character, from text values in the context (not paraphrased). Do not propose actions, settings or code changes. Answer with one JSON object that matches response_schema and nothing else.
